_comment: Guided tour for the ChiSurf console. Every step that asks for something waits for the user to type it; the tour never types on their behalf, because someone who watched a line being run has not learned to run one. Walkable on an empty session -- no data, no fits, no files needed. Read by chisurf.gui.widgets.tools.guided_tour.

steps.title: This is the same session you are looking at
steps.text:
The console is a Python prompt inside the running application — not a separate one. Every dataset you have loaded and every fit you have open is reachable from here, and anything you do takes effect immediately.

Seven short steps. You do the typing; the tour only points.

steps.title: Try it
steps.text:
Click in the console and type

2 + 40

then press Enter. The value comes back under an Out[1]: label. A statement — x = 1 — prints nothing, exactly as Python behaves.

steps.title: cs is the application
steps.text:
The name cs is the whole chisurf package. Type

cs.fits

and press Enter. On an empty session that is an empty list — which is the point: it is the real list, and it fills as you open fits.

Also in scope: gui (the main window), np, os, and _ for the last result.

steps.title: Tab completes against the live objects
steps.text:
Type cs. and press Tab. The list is built by asking the object what it actually has, right now — so it works for things no static analyser could know, like the columns of a DataFrame or the parameters of a model you just built.

Shift+Tab inside a call shows its signature instead.

await.hint: Type cs. and press Tab. Esc closes the list.

steps.title: Ask what something is
steps.text:
Put a question mark after anything:

cs.fits?

Type it and press Enter. The type, signature and docstring open in a pane below the console rather than filling the transcript. ?? shows the source as well.

Press Esc or q to close the pane.

await.hint: Type cs.fits? and press Enter, then Esc to close the pane.

steps.title: Blocks, history and interrupting
steps.text:
Typing for i in range(3): and pressing Enter gives a continuation line, already indented; a blank line ends the block and runs it.

Up and Down walk what you have typed, filtered by the start of the line. Ctrl+R searches it. Ctrl+C interrupts a command that is taking too long, and a runaway print loop cannot lock the window — output is capped, with a note saying how much was dropped.

steps.title: Turning what you did into a script
steps.text:
Macro ▸ Record in the menu bar starts collecting everything you run. Click it again to stop, and it offers to save the lot as a .py file.

Replay it later with %run -i thatfile.py — the -i matters: it runs in this namespace, so the variables it makes stay available.

%quickref is the one-page summary of everything else.
